text.p: Kaiser Aluminum & Chemical Corp said Friday it has modified plans to increase capacity of heat-treated flat-rolled products at its Trentwood, Wash., rolling mill to about 130 million pounds from about 100 million pounds.
Spokesman Scott Lamb said strength in demand for heat treated products from the aerospace industry was behind the changes.
Kaiser said the planned capacity expansion of 30 million pounds per year to 130 million pounds will be brought on line in phases instead of all at once by the end of 1998.
The company said the earliest benefits are now expected to be realized in the fourth quarter of 1997.
Lamb said "the bulk" of the expansion is now expected to be in operation sooner than the late 1998 original target.

Kaiser announced in May 1996 it would spend about $45 million to expand heat-treated production. The project envisioned construction of a new facility near Trentwood as well as modifications of that facility.
The company, which is 62 percent owned by MAXXAM Inc, also said the modification is expected to result in greater capital productivity.
Explaining the revised plan, Kaiser said it has determined it can achieve or exceed the targeted production capacity increase without construction of a new facility.
Instead, the company will modify its existing facility and, as a result, expects the project's capital productivity to be improved.
Lamb said the overall capital cost is still expected to be about the same as the announced $45 million.

"Based on our strategic review of this project, and on Trentwood's improved performance over the last several months, we have concluded that we can build on our existing heat-treat capabilities in-house faster and more effectively than originally thought," said Raymond Milchovich, president of Kaiser Flat-Rolled Products.

"We expect that the decision to invest internally will enable us to address more quickly the needs of our customers and that the revised project will provide an even greater increase in production capacity of this high value-added product."
The revised project also includes additional plans to broaden the company's product offering and allows for newly identified quality improvements in Trentwood's heat-treat product flow, Kaiser said.

Trentwood is Kaiser's largest fabricating plant and the only multipurpose aluminum rolling mill in the western United States. In addition to its production of heat-treated products for the aerospace and general engineering markets, it produces a variety of other sheet and plate products, including sheet for beverage cans and products for the automotive and industrial markets.
